record.source_closeout_reference: Authored during the mission in the Claude Code session executing the sponsor-approved long-running-mission gap plan; committed with the mission changes per the same_commit convention

mission.objective: Plan a narrow live trial of a vendor-native interrupt transport: one answered Tier 3 round-trip and one deliberate timeout exercising the no-response safe-hold rule, fully recorded and transport-independent, with trial execution gated on separate sponsor approval.

envelope.reference: Sponsor agreement with the five-gap analysis and instruction to address the gaps in sequence starting with the next three or four bounded missions
envelope.not_created_reason: Bounded docs-only change executed from a direct thread-local sponsor instruction; this shadow record was authored during the mission.

forbidden_scope: no live transport use, bot, token, polling, webhook, or messaging
allowed_commands: scoped git add, commit, and push after approval
fallback_triggers: scope expands beyond the trial plan, registry read-first path, and README bullet
any wording implies live transport use is approved by the plan itself
the plan weakens any spike-era prohibition
verification reports an unresolved advisory finding

verification.summary: Advisory lint, NL pilot, knowledge lint, and diff whitespace checks passed on the first run after the edits; mission-record lint run after this record was authored.

notes: Docs-only plan with no new dependencies, transport code, or live integration.
The plan preserves every spike-era prohibition and adds an explicit separate-approval gate naming transport, mission, window, and human.
Deliberate-timeout design means the safe-hold rule gets exercised under controlled conditions rather than discovered under real failure.
Scope stayed inside the trial plan, registry path, and README bullet.
No transport, credential, or unattended scope was added.

friction_notes: The trial depends on vendor transport behavior (Remote Control delivery, push notifications) that V3 cannot pin; the plan treats transport failure as valid evidence to keep the trial honest under vendor churn.
Latency measurement requires command-sourced timestamps on both sides of a human answer; the deliver-to-answer interval includes human response time and must not be read as transport latency.
false_positive_notes: No advisory findings were raised on this change.
false_negative_notes: No false negatives observed after the advisory pass.

phase2_design_signals: Designing the timeout path as a deliberate trial step turns the scariest long-running failure mode (unanswered human) into rehearsed, recorded behavior.
Transport-independence of the interrupt record is the testable claim inherited from the spike; the trial operationalizes it as a pass criterion.
A failed delivery being valid evidence keeps incentives honest: the mission is graded on halting cleanly, not on the vendor behaving.
